title: CPU Path Tracer
oneLiner: A physically accurate renderer written from scratch in C++.
claim: Renders global illumination on the CPU alone, with no graphics API underneath it.

metrics: BVH traversal cuts ray intersection from O(N) to O(log N)
Up to 100+ primary rays per pixel for stochastic supersampling
10 light bounces tracked recursively with per-hit material attenuation
The image buffer is split into horizontal chunks across cores with std::thread

media.alt: A CPU path-traced render of a test scene, showing soft shadows, refracted glass and coloured light bounce
media.caption: Rendered on the CPU. The only dependency is the C++ standard library.

proof.architecture: A custom vector maths library feeds a look-at camera that mimics a real lens. Rays hit a bounding volume hierarchy of axis-aligned boxes; on a hit the path either scatters by material - Lambertian, metallic or dielectric through Snell's law - or attenuates and continues, up to ten bounces deep.
